title: Per-customer Terraform feature gates and safe upgrade orchestration
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Goal: Define and implement a repeatable pattern for per-customer Terraform customizations that enables: (1) safe, observable module upgrades with rollback hooks, (2) opt-in/out feature gates for tenant-level toggles, and (3) overlay composition without duplicating upstream modules. Problem: customers request small custom network/security tweaks that diverge from the standard module. Current approaches either fork modules (hard to upgrade) or overwrite variables (hard to validate). We need a middle ground that is upgrade-friendly and auditable. Approach: 1) Introduce a small, stable 'extension' module that hosts customer-specific resources and can be composed into our base tenant module via a documented interface. 2) Implement a feature_gates map variable on the tenant module to enable/disable optional features (e.g., dedicated-nat, custom-route-maps, extra-firewall-rules). 3) Use semantic module versioning + an upgrade orchestration plan that runs pre-upgrade health checks, incremental apply in canary workspaces, and a post-upgrade verification step with automatic rollback on failed checks. 4) Provide a validation lint step in CI (terratest + tflint rules) to catch malformed overlays and disallowed APIs. This ticket covers design, implementation of the pattern in one example customer repo (acme-corp-iac), and an initial rollout script in the infra-ci pipeline.
tasks: Design extension module interface and variable contract
Implement feature_gates variable and default gate matrix in base tenant module
Create canary workspace orchestration script in infra-ci
Add pre/post health checks using runtime probes (API endpoints + k8s readiness)
Write terratest suite covering overlay behavior and rollback cases
Document pattern with examples and migration guide for existing customers
acceptance_criteria: A customer repo (acme-corp-iac) demonstrates a non-fork overlay using extension module and passes CI
Module versions can be upgraded via infra-ci where canary workspace apply runs first and shows health checks green before promotion
Feature gates documented; toggling a gate results in deterministic plan diffs and is reversible
TFLint/terratest catches an injected invalid overlay and CI fails with actionable message
Rollback triggers on health check failure and recorded in audit log with a link to incident runbook
